question: Which of the following Buddhist sages had initiated the Indo-Greek king Menander into Buddhism?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagasena**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​__The** Buddhist monk Nagasena converted the Indo-Greek king Menander to Buddhism.** 
 
• The conversion is** documented in the Pali Buddhist text Milinda-panha.**
 
• **Menander was an Indo-Greek king and ruler of Bact**ria.
 
• He was also known as Milinda. 
 
• Nagasena** was a Buddhist monk and philosopher. **
 
• **The Milinda-panha is a Pali Buddhist text that records** a dialogue between Menander and Nagasena.
 
• The dialogue ends with Menander converting to Buddhism. 
 
• Menander w**as a patron of Buddhism and the wheel on his coins is connected with Buddhism. **
 
• **After converting to Buddhism, Menander sent Buddhist missionaries to Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Vasubandhu
 4th–5th century CE
 Buddhist scholar and philosopher; associated with Mahayana Buddhism.
 Abhidharmakośa; Yogācāra texts (with Asaṅga).
 
 

 Aśvaghoṣa
 1st–2nd century CE
 Indian philosopher, poet, and playwright; earliest Sanskrit dramatist.
 Buddhacharita, Saundarananda.
 
 

 Śāriputra
 6th–5th century BCE
 Chief disciple of Gautama Buddha; known for wisdom and mastery of Abhidharma.
 Mentioned in early Buddhist scriptures like the Tripiṭaka.
